title: Customer Feedback Compass — Q4 2026 (annotated)
summary: This is an annotated synthesis of customer feedback collected in Q4 2026 (Oct 1 — Nov 10). Inputs: 18 customer interviews (CSM-run), 420 support tickets flagged as "feature ask", two live pilot retrospective writeups, and telemetry signal triangulation (latency spikes + error traces). Goal: produce a compact set of prioritized feature requests and hypothesis-driven recommendations for product and engineering to act on during the Q1 roadmap planning window. This doc mixes polished bullets with working notes and unresolved questions (notes-to-self style).
key_insights: Operational predictability > raw throughput for most enterprise customers: predictable tail latency and clear fallbacks matter more than peak qps improvements.
Billing opacity: customers want per-route and per-model token cost transparency that maps to product routes (not just aggregated invoices).
Private deployments still struggle with autoscaling ergonomics: teams prefer deterministic buffer sizing and clearer failure modes rather than fully automatic scaling that sometimes hides issues.
Fallback & quality: customers want configurable fallback policies that respect cost/quality tradeoffs (e.g., degrade to smaller quantized model vs. block requests).
Observability asks skew toward developer workflows: token-level traces, per-request prompt/response sampling (PII-safe), and quick correlation between SDK calls and infra traces.
feature_requests: Route-aware billing export: export per-route, per-model, per-environment token usage CSVs. Ask came from 8 customers; concrete ask: mapping to internal product route ids.
Deterministic autoscale profiles for Private: UI to pin buffer targets and simulate scale events before applying. Customers called out three incidents where autoscale oscillation caused request loss.
Graceful multi-tier fallback policies: a policy DSL to define fallback chains (model -> quantized model -> cached response) and SLO violations that trigger them.
Per-request cost attribution tag: SDK header that carries product-specific tags; feature to show costing per tag in console and billing export.
Token-trace sampling for dev builds: sampled traces with redaction helper; customers want 1% sampling in staging and 0.01% in prod with easy PII redaction controls.
Model-version rollout dashboard: show traffic % by model version, per-route latency delta, and automatic regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
Edge-region policy: allow routing control by customer to prefer region A for latency-sensitive routes and region B for cheaper capacity during off-peak.
customer_quotes: "We'd rather lose 10% throughput but never see 500ms tail spikes — predictability is king." — Director of AI, fintech customer
"Billing emails arrive as blobs. We need to reconcile charges to our product features, not opaque token buckets." — Engineering manager, ecommerce platform
"Autoscale silently drained our warm cache during a holiday sale and we paid for the outage. A simulation tool would have saved us." — Infra lead, direct-to-consumer startup
prioritization_rationale: Shortlist rationale: prioritize features that reduce customer pain with a clear engineering scope and measurable ROI. First wave (P0/P1) should be: Route-aware billing export, Model-version rollout dashboard, and Graceful multi-tier fallback. These address the largest frequency/impact signals (billing confusion, rollout regressions, outages). Autoscale profiles and token-trace sampling are P2: high value but require more infra work and privacy review.
unresolved_questions: Privacy boundary for token-trace sampling: acceptable PII redaction rules (customer legal to confirm)
Billing mapping: do we retroactively map historic usage to product route ids or start from implementation date only?
Fallback QoS tradeoffs: should fallback decisions be per-tenant or global defaults?
Edge-region pricing model: do we surface different unit-prices per region in the console?
